question: Salil’s salary was first reduced by 25% and subsequently raised by 12%. What percentage was his final salary lower than his initial salary?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive percentage change can be calculated directly using the formula: x + y + (x × y) / 100

Here, reduction x = −25% and raise y = +12%

⇒ Net Change = −25 + 12 + (−25 × 12) / 100

⇒ Net Change = −13 − (300 / 100)

⇒ Net Change = −13 − 3 = −16%

The negative sign indicates an overall decrease of 16%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First percentage change = 25% reduction

Second percentage change = 12% raise

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 − Reduction / 100) × (1 + Raise / 100)
